description: DDL, input, canonical output, casts, and catalog OIDs for built-in range types
sql: CREATE TABLE type_matrix_range (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, ints INT4RANGE, bigints INT8RANGE, exacts NUMRANGE, days DATERANGE, local_times TSRANGE, instants TSTZRANGE);
SELECT ints, bigints, exacts, days, local_times, instants FROM type_matrix_range WHERE id = 'r1';

SELECT '[1,5)'::int4range AS ints, '[9007199254740993,9007199254741000)'::int8range AS bigints, '[0.10,9.90]'::numrange AS exacts, '[2024-01-01,2024-02-01)'::daterange AS days, '[2024-01-01,2024-01-02)'::tsrange AS local_times, '[2024-01-01,2024-01-02)'::tstzrange AS instants;

SELECT '[1,5]'::int4range AS inclusive_ints, '(1,5)'::int4range AS exclusive_ints, '(1,1]'::int4range AS empty_ints, '[9007199254740993,9007199254741000]'::int8range AS inclusive_bigints, '[2024-01-01,2024-01-31]'::daterange AS inclusive_days;

SELECT a.attname, a.atttypid, pg_catalog.format_type(a.atttypid, a.atttypmod) AS formatted_type FROM pg_catalog.pg_attribute a JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class c ON c.oid = a.attrelid WHERE c.relname = 'type_matrix_range' AND a.attnum > 0 ORDER BY a.attnum;
